# v2.38 Release Notes

## The performance release: fast at any size

This stable release rolls up the dev pre-releases **v2.33-dev … v2.38-dev** — a
full, multi-phase performance project. The goal throughout was to keep the app
fast as your data and your team grow, **with no change to how anything looks or
what any number says**. Every affected report was verified to produce
byte-identical results before and after; the only visible additions are
pagination controls on the two largest report tables.

No action is required to benefit from any of this. One database migration runs on
update and it **only adds indexes** — no data is changed or moved.

### Faster queries as data grows

- **Database indexes on the busiest tables.** Completions are now indexed by
  training, expiry date and completion date, and students by country and theatre,
  so PostgreSQL jumps straight to the matching rows instead of scanning more of
  the table as it fills up.
- **Fewer database round-trips in reports.** *Trained But Not Certified*, *Legacy
  Replacement Gap* and the *partner-program compliance* dashboards used to fire a
  burst of queries per training/theatre; they now batch that into a handful of
  queries. *Achieved in Last 12 Months* filters in the database instead of loading
  all history first.
- **Tunable connection pool.** The app opens up to 20 database connections by
  default (was 10), so simultaneous heavy reports queue less. Adjust with the
  optional `DATABASE_POOL_MAX` setting.

### Shared, short-lived caching (better under load)

- **Concurrent viewers share one computation.** The dashboard, the heavier
  reports, and the partner-program compliance dashboards cache their results for a
  few seconds, so ten people opening the same page trigger the database work
  **once**. A burst of identical requests collapses to a single round-trip, and
  back/forward navigation can reuse the last response.
- **Always current after a change.** The cache is scoped per company and view and
  is cleared immediately whenever underlying data changes (adding/editing a
  record, an import, or partner-program setup) — so you never see stale numbers
  right after an edit.
- **Optional `REPORT_CACHE_TTL_MS`** tunes the cache lifetime (default 30s; `0`
  disables it).

### Heavy report pages now scale to any size

The three largest report pages used to download whole datasets into your browser
and crunch them there. They now compute on the server (cached) and send only a
small, ready-made result:

- **Currently Expired** and **Learner Achievement Scorecard** — charts, KPI cards,
  leaderboards and group subtotals are computed server-side, and their detail
  tables are now **paginated** (page through with the controls beneath the table).
  All filters, toggles, sorting and grouping behave exactly as before, and
  **exports still contain the full filtered set**, not just the visible page.
- **Theatre / Region / Country Comparison** — the per-geography matrix and charts
  are computed on the server. (No pagination here — the matrix is one row per
  geography.)

### Fewer duplicate requests per page load

- The theatre/region/country reference list is now fetched **once per session**
  and shared across the pages that use it, instead of each page re-requesting it.
- The current-user lookup (`/api/auth/me`, a database read) was being requested
  twice on every protected page; those two now **share one request**.

### Notes

- **Migration:** one index-only migration runs on update (a one-time cost on very
  large tables; no data changes).
- **Configuration:** none required. `DATABASE_POOL_MAX` and `REPORT_CACHE_TTL_MS`
  are optional tuning knobs.
- **No functional or visual changes** beyond the new pagination controls on the
  Currently Expired and Learner Achievement Scorecard tables.
